QF.id: Taxation of Debt and Equity Products_C2_4

question.text: Scenario: Suresh Iyer, aged 55, is a resident Indian with total taxable income of Rs. 16,00,000 (in the 20% slab under new regime FY 2025-26, effective marginal rate approximately 20% plus cess). He is evaluating five investment options for a lump sum of Rs. 10,00,000 with a horizon of just over 2 years (assume the holding period exceeds 24 months for every option): Option 1: Bank Fixed Deposit at 7.5% p.a. (compounded annually). Interest taxable at slab rate. Option 2: Listed Corporate Bond (NCD) yielding 8% p.a. coupon (paid annually). If held >12 months and sold, LTCG at 12.5%. Option 3: Equity Mutual Fund with expected NAV growth of 12% p.a. (no dividend). If held >12 months, LTCG at 12.5% above Rs. 1.25 lakh under s.112A. Option 4: Gold Mutual Fund with expected NAV growth of 10% p.a. Holding period assumed to exceed 24 months, so LTCG at 12.5% without indexation under section 112. Option 5: Debt Mutual Fund (85% in debt, purchased after 1-Apr-2023) with expected NAV growth of 7.5% p.a. Always taxed as STCG at slab rate under s.50AA. Assume: New tax regime with no deductions. Suresh's marginal tax rate for additional income is 20% (in the Rs. 16-20 lakh slab). Ignore surcharge. Health & Education cess is 4%. Effective marginal rate = 20% x 1.04 = 20.8%. For s.112A, assume no other LTCG, so Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption is available. For Option 4, treat the 2-year pre-tax compounding as approximating the more-than-24-month holding period (1.10^2 = 1.21). Question 4 of 5: What is the post-tax maturity value and approximate post-tax CAGR from the Gold Mutual Fund (Option 4) assuming the holding period exceeds 24 months?

answer.text: Post-tax value approximately Rs. 11,82,700; post-tax CAGR approximately 8.8% p.a.
Post-tax value approximately Rs. 12,10,000; post-tax CAGR approximately 10.0% p.a.
Post-tax value approximately Rs. 11,66,320; post-tax CAGR approximately 7.9% p.a.
Post-tax value approximately Rs. 11,73,750; post-tax CAGR approximately 8.4% p.a.

explanation.text: The Logic: Step-by-step computation for the Gold Mutual Fund (holding period assumed >24 months per the stem): Step 1 - Pre-tax maturity value (NAV growth of 10% p.a.): Rs. 10,00,000 x (1.10)^2 = Rs. 12,10,000. Step 2 - Capital gain: LTCG = Rs. 12,10,000 - Rs. 10,00,000 = Rs. 2,10,000. Holding >24 months qualifies as long-term for gold mutual funds, so LTCG is taxed at 12.5% without indexation under section 112 (post Budget 2024). Step 3 - Tax on LTCG: Gold MFs do not get the Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption under s.112A (that exemption is only for equity-oriented funds with STT). Tax rate with 4% cess = 12.5% x 1.04 = 13%. Tax = 13% x Rs. 2,10,000 = Rs. 27,300. Step 4 - Post-tax maturity value: Rs. 12,10,000 - Rs. 27,300 = Rs. 11,82,700. Step 5 - Post-tax CAGR: (11,82,700 / 10,00,000)^(1/2) - 1 = approximately 8.8% p.a. The Trap: Option B shows the pre-tax value with no tax deducted. Option C uses the slab rate (20.8%) instead of 12.5% LTCG. Option D applies an incorrect rate or indexation. The audit flagged the original stem because "2-year horizon" combined with "holding >24 months" was ambiguous - exactly 24 months is not strictly more than 24 months, and the keyed answer collapses if the holding period is not long-term. Note: The original stem mixed "2-year horizon" with "Holding >24 months" without dates. The stem has been tightened to expressly assume the holding period exceeds 24 months and to note that the 1.10^2 compounding is being used as a close approximation. With that disambiguation, the Rs. 11,82,700 / 8.8% CAGR calculation using 12.5% LTCG plus 4% cess is uniquely supported (NISM Series X-B pp.257, 287-288).
